text:
jordan: Heads-up — ran into a weird case while testing multi-region routing for VIP customers. traffic from APAC is getting routed to eu-west when the us-west pool is overloaded, but the model-variant fallback picks a quantized v-small that regresses on a few of our eval prompts.

maria: Ugh. Is that because the routing priority only considers latency probe + capacity and not tier-aware model quality?

jordan: Exactly. Our current rule: prefer region with lowest probe-latency unless capacity < 20% then fallback tier. That doesn't include per-customer model-quality thresholds.

alex: Can you paste the config? we might be able to add a per-customer override.

jordan: Here — simplified snippet from the test config:

```
routing:
  region_priority:
    - name: us-west
      weight: 1.0
    - name: eu-west
      weight: 0.8
  probe_window_s: 30
  capacity_threshold_pct: 20
fallback_policy:
  prefer_lower_latency: true
  variant_order: [v-large, v-medium, v-small]
  allow_quantized: true
```

jordan: Problem is allow_quantized=true for VIP customers causes v-small to be selected in eu-west even though it fails some quality checks.

priya: We should add a "min_quality_score" that is evaluated per-variant and per-customer tier. VIPs require >=0.92 on the canonical eval set. If a candidate region only has variants below that, don't route there.

max: Agree. Also think about adding a small latency penalty when crossing regions for stateful sessions — i.e., prefer local region unless quality delta > X.

maria: +1 to both. For the console UX, we should surface why a request was routed to a non-preferred region (tooltip: "Fallback reason: variant_quality<min for us-west; selected eu-west variant v-small").

ajex: (typo, ignore)

alex: We also need telemetry: per-request routing decision + snapshot of the top 3 candidates (region, variant, estimated latency, quality_score). That will make debugging easier. Keep the payload small, something like:

```
{"candidates": [{"region":"us-west","variant":"v-large","latency_ms":45,"quality":0.95},
               {"region":"eu-west","variant":"v-small","latency_ms":65,"quality":0.86}],
 "final": {"region":"eu-west","variant":"v-small","reason":"us-west_quality_below_threshold"}}
```

priya: For SLOs we should avoid exposing raw quality numbers in logs for customer privacy, but hashed eval ids or boolean pass/fail is ok. Maybe store quality scores in internal telemetry only.

jordan: Good point. Do we want to block routing decisions that would pick a variant that fails the tier threshold, or just prefer alternatives and only block as last resort?

max: I'd block for VIPs. For standard tiers, prefer alternatives but allow fallback if latency delta > Y ms. Config knobs: block_threshold_per_tier and soft_penalty_ms.

maria: Can we add a simulation mode in the console rollout page — simulate routing with current live metrics + hypothetical variant availability so PMs can see how many VIP requests would be affected by a change?

alex: Implementation notes: we can add a new selector in routing engine: evaluate candidates by score = weighted(latency_rank, capacity_rank, quality_pass). quality_pass is binary for tier. Keep it cheap — use cached eval results and avoid per-request heavyweight checks.

priya: For rollout UX, add a canary toggle: "enforce-tier-quality" with % rollout. So we can slowly enforce VIP blocking before flipping global.

jordan: +1. Also noticed devops-bot reported a spike on the eu-west pool when this happened:

"devops-bot: [alert] 2026-07-09T14:12:03Z eu-west pool utilization 94% (recent spike) — triggered traffic overflow to eu-west-aux"

maria: If we implement blocking for VIPs, we should add an automatic fallback to dedicated capacity or queueing rather than cross-region fallback, to avoid quality regressions.

max: Queueing for VIPs is a good pattern if latency budget allows. We should expose "max_queue_ms_per_tier" in route configs.

alex: Action items: (1) add min_quality_score per-tier, per-variant policy in routing config (2) include candidate snapshot in telemetry (hashed/flagged for privacy) (3) console UX: simulate + canary toggle + tooltip explanations (4) add queue/dedicated fallback option for blocked requests.

jordan: I'll open a PR with the config changes and telemetry schema mock. tagging: @maria @priya for review.

priya: Happy to review. Can we also add a short integration test that simulates variant-quality failures across regions? simple harness should do.

alex: I'll wire the console bits after PR lands. Thanks everyone :rocket:
